original_query: SELECT SUM(CAST(t3.f1 * t4.SAL AS INTEGER)) FROM (SELECT SAL, COUNT(*) AS f1 FROM EMP GROUP BY SAL) AS t3 INNER JOIN (SELECT SAL FROM EMP GROUP BY SAL) AS t4 ON t3.SAL = t4.SAL
rewritten_query: SELECT SUM(SAL) AS total_salary FROM EMP

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Removed the redundant t4 subquery (SELECT SAL FROM EMP GROUP BY SAL) since t3 already contains one row per distinct SAL; the self-join on SAL only re-matches each distinct salary to itself and adds a costly Merge Join over two 45M-row aggregations.

Since EMP.SAL is integer (plan shows width=4), COUNT(*) * SAL per SAL group mathematically equals the sum of SAL values in that group; summing across all groups equals SUM(SAL) over the whole table. The GROUP BY, self-join, and per-group cast are all eliminated, reducing the query to a single aggregation (NULL salaries are ignored by SUM, matching the original join which excluded the NULL group).
